## Motivation

Cross-request image batching in `mm_schedule.py` merges same-round per-image
cache misses into a single ViT forward, amortizing kernel launch/scheduling
overhead. NPU was fenced off from this path (grouped with HIP/XPU onto the
per-request path); the code comment cites a ROCm regression and a conservative
blanket disable — there is no NPU-specific measurement behind it.

Qwen3-VL is a safe candidate to open up: its `get_image_feature` natively
accepts a list of `MultimodalDataItem` and packs multiple images' `grid_thw`
into one visual forward, so no model-side change is needed. The existing
CUDA-path guarantees carry over: dedup by `(hash, token_count)`, embedding
cache backfill, and `sort_by_req_idx` reassembly keep every request's outputs
attached to its own images.

While validating on NPU we also found the batched encode call has no bound:
every cache miss in a scheduling round goes into one ViT forward, so workspace
scales with arrival burstiness (a wave of large images can spike several GB).
This PR therefore also adds a per-call ViT token budget to cap it.

## Modifications

1. **`mm_schedule.py`: open cross-request batching for NPU + Qwen3-VL.**
   Replace the blanket `_is_hip or _is_npu or _is_xpu` check with
   `_can_batch_cross_request_image_misses()`: CUDA unchanged; HIP/XPU stay on
   the per-request path; NPU is enabled only for
   `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` and `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration`
   (dense verified on device; MoE shares the same `get_image_feature`
   interface). `is_per_image` admission and the split/backfill logic are
   untouched.
2. **`environ.py` + `mm_schedule.py`: per-call ViT token budget.**
   New `SGLANG_MM_CROSS_REQUEST_BATCH_TOKEN_BUDGET` (default 4096, `<=0`
   disables). `_chunk_misses_by_token_budget()` greedily splits cache misses
   into groups whose total token count fits the budget and encodes them one
   group per call; an oversized single image forms its own group.
   Dedup/backfill/cache logic is unchanged.
3. Unit tests for the batched path (two requests merged into one call, outputs
   asserted split-per-request and equal to per-request reference).

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py`:
  **29 passed** (run in-container on Ascend 910).
- End-to-end A/B on Ascend 910 / Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (CANN 9.1.0-a3): 8
  fixed-seed image cases, identical inputs across baseline (per-request) and
  treatment (batched), `max_tokens=48`. **No cross-request contamination** —
  every caption describes its own image. 5/8 cases show benign wording drift
  after ~30 tokens ("identifiable/recognizable" level), expected from
  batch-variant numerics (reduction order changes); batching is not
  bit-invariant by design.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment: Ascend 910 (64GB HBM), CANN 9.1.0-a3, Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct,
`--attention-backend ascend --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests
64`, `mem-fraction-static 0.80` unless noted. Repo-standard
`sglang.bench_serving` with the `image` dataset (unique random JPEG per
request, all cache misses), same seed for A/B rounds; the only difference
between rounds is `mm_schedule.py`.

| Workload | TTFT mean | TTFT p99 | Throughput | E2E mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448², out=32, c16 | 1190 → 629 ms (**-47%**) | 5143 → 2467 ms (-52%) | 9.19 → 13.83 req/s (**+50%**) | -34% |
| 448², out=32, c32 | 3508 → 548 ms (**-84%**) | 5304 → 644 ms (-88%) | 7.60 → 27.68 req/s (**+264%**) | -73% |
| 1920×1080, out=256, c42 | 7496 → 7356 ms (-1.9%) | 14584 → 12831 ms (**-12%**) | 2.06 → 2.12 req/s (+2.4%) | -2.9% |
| 1920×1080, out=256, c16 | 3007 → 2995 ms (±0.4%) | 4546 → 4529 ms (±0.4%) | 4.64 → 4.67 req/s (+0.6%) | ±0.5% |
| Mixed 448²+1080p (16+16 c), small side | 1069 → 648 ms (**-39%**) | 3819 → 3479 ms (-9%) | 6.21 → 7.28 req/s (**+17%**) | -15% |
| Mixed, large side | 3705 → 3332 ms (-10%) | 6868 → 6235 ms (-9%) | 2.80 → 3.02 req/s (+8%) | -7% |

ViT call count (mechanism evidence):

| Workload | Baseline | Batched |
|---|---|---|
| 1080p c42 | 153 calls, all single-image | 48 calls for 153 images, max 4-in-1 |
| 448² c32 | 128 calls | 16 calls, max **19-in-1** |
| Mixed | 385+192 calls | 75+57 calls, incl. 3 genuine mixed batches (8S+1L ×2, 2S+4L) |

Findings:
- Gains scale with per-image ViT token count (small = more launch overhead to
  amortize), decode share (dilutes prefill gains), and same-round batchable
  images (arrival pattern). Small images + short outputs + high concurrency is
  the sweet spot; large images under steady pressure gain 2~4% with the best
  tail improvement (p99 -12%).
- Mixed workloads: net win with a bounded convoy effect — ~6% of small-image
  requests overlapping a large-image ViT window see TTFT dragged to ~3.5 s
  (one large-image ViT duration, hard-capped; p50 unaffected at 422 ms). The
  baseline per-request path shows the same effect at higher severity (9.4% of
  requests >3 s vs 5.8% batched), so this is not introduced by batching.
- Concurrency <4: no gain (low-concurrency sweep measured; knee between 4–8).

Memory:
- Batched ViT workspace adds ~+0.9 GB (64140 → 65074 MiB, large-image c8).
- At `mem-fraction-static 0.85` the large-image workload OOMs **with or
  without** the token budget — root cause identified via traceback as the
  8192-token prefill chunk's LLM attention workspace
  (`forward_extend` → `_npu_flash_attention_qlens` failing to allocate
  180 MiB with 37 MiB free), not the ViT batch.
- 0.85 + budget + `--chunked-prefill-size 4096` survives the same workload
  (0 OOM, c8 TTFT 1.63 s ≈ 0.80 baseline). Recommended configurations:
  `0.80 + budget` (safe default) or `0.85 + budget + chunk 4096` (reclaims
  ~3.2 GB KV pool).

Token budget cost: none on the hot path (small-image c32 still hits 20-in-1 =
3920 tokens, TTFT within run-to-run variance of no-limit: 617 vs 548 ms with
same-code repeats at 753/617 ms); large-image batches cap at 2-in-1
(3528 tokens), halving per-call workspace with c8 TTFT unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the contribution guide (pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests (`test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py`, 29 passed).
- [ ] Update documentation (env var to be added to docs if required).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (see above; raw
      bench jsonl / ViT call logs / npu-smi samples archived).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style.

### Collaboration update: input-patch budget + A2 validation

I have integrated the input-patch budgeting and regression coverage from #44233 into this branch as incremental, signed-off commit `3e50dc742b` (preserving the original commits).

**Configuration and scope**
- Replace the merged-output-token budget with `SGLANG_NPU_VIT_MAX_BATCH_PATCHES`, counting **input patches before spatial merging**. With merge size 2, 16384 input patches correspond to 4096 output visual tokens. Output token counts are still used to split embeddings correctly.
- **Default is 0 (disabled)**; positive values opt in. Nonpositive values disable NPU cross-request batching, rather than removing the limit. This is intentional: the A2 measurements below show workload-dependent throughput regressions.
- Retain the Qwen3-VL Dense/MoE allowlist, with conservative guards for TP=1, unquantized models, no encoder DP, and ViT graphs disabled. Unsupported configurations retain per-request encoding. CUDA batching is unchanged.
- Oversized/unknown-size images run alone; the budget is **not a hard memory cap**. Inputs are moved per group.

**A2 serving performance**

Environment: one Ascend 910B3 64 GB (A2), CANN 9.0.0, PyTorch/torch-npu 2.10.0, Transformers 5.12.1 from the A2 image, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct BF16, TP1, eager, chunked prefill 4096, context 8192, max-running-requests 64, mem-fraction-static 0.7. This is a different hardware/software/model setup from the original A3/4B measurements, so the numbers should not be compared directly.

Tool: repository-standard `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name image`; unique random JPEGs, one image/request, 32 requested text tokens, fixed output length, unlimited request rate bounded by the listed concurrency. Two rounds with matched seeds across arms; server restarted between disabled (0) and enabled (16384). Each arm was warmed by the preceding accuracy pass; per-run benchmark warmup was 0 and prefix cache was flushed. Different seeds avoid repeated-image cache hits between workloads.

Numbers below are the **arithmetic mean of two run-level summaries** (including per-run P99, not a pooled P99). These are measurements on a shared server, not confidence intervals or universal speedup guarantees.

| Workload | Requests/round | Mean TTFT ms, off → on | P99 TTFT ms, off → on | Throughput req/s, off → on | Mean E2E ms, off → on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 448×448, output 32, c4 | 64 | 471 → 378 (-19.7%) | 518 → 419 | 1.709 → 1.815 (+6.2%) | 2335 → 2197 |
| 448×448, output 32, c16 | 128 | 1487 → 859 (-42.3%) | 2793 → 990 | 4.566 → 4.279 (**-6.3%**) | 3496 → 3722 |
| 448×448, output 32, c32 | 128 | 2358 → 1328 (-43.7%) | 2729 → 1646 | 5.564 → 7.193 (+29.3%) | 5726 → 4423 |
| 1920×1080, output 256, c16 | 64 | 5482 → 5080 (-7.3%) | 8679 → 7425 | 0.671 → 0.519 (**-22.6%**) | 23740 → 30707 |

All **1536 measured requests** completed successfully, with no observed OOM. The main conclusion is improved small-image TTFT, **not** a blanket throughput improvement. In particular, the large-image regression repeated in both rounds; this is why the integration keeps the optimization opt-in. No new peak-memory claim is made.

**Paired real-image accuracy**

192 fixed images: 64 each from ChartQA, DocVQA, and VQAv2; identical inputs, concurrency 8, temperature 0, seed 42, max_tokens 64, longest image edge capped at 1024.

| Subset metric | Disabled | Enabled |
|---|---:|---:|
| ChartQA relaxed score | 0.859375 | 0.859375 |
| DocVQA ANLS | 0.920980 | 0.936605 |
| VQAv2 majority-answer EM | 0.671875 | 0.671875 |

190/192 answer strings were exactly identical. The other two changed: ChartQA 1.89 → reference 1.88 (both pass the relaxed metric), and one DocVQA wrong answer → reference “midwestern”. No API failures or truncated outputs. This is a small-subset regression check, **not** proof of universal precision parity, bitwise-equivalent embeddings, or improved general model accuracy. VQAv2 uses majority-answer EM, not the official consensus metric.

**Tests and documentation**
- CPU regression suite: **36 passed**, including input/output budget distinction, oversized/unknown shapes, cache on/off, continuation slices, default-off behavior, and mode guards.
- Single-NPU E2E: **1 passed** on A2, independently launching the final commit with budget 2048 and chunk size 512; covers mixed sizes, multi-image order, oversized images, and cache reuse.
- pre-commit, `mint validate`, and `mint broken-links`: passed.
- Added the NPU environment-variable documentation and a registered single-NPU image-association/cache E2E.

One unrelated environment caveat: the current branch's NPU image preprocessing calls the older `resize(image=...)` interface. In our isolated Transformers 5.19 environment, startup failed before batching with `Qwen2VLImageProcessor.resize() missing ... images and factor`; the A2 image's Transformers 5.12.1 works. No preprocessing compatibility patch is included in this integration.

@Suxing224: I can push to your branch but cannot edit this PR's upstream description. Please update the configuration/default and test sections from the details above, and label the existing A3 results as measurements of the earlier revision. Raw per-run JSONL, server logs, and paired accuracy outputs have been retained for follow-up.

**CI follow-up:** the new [title check](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39220835232) rejects the existing title format (this is a metadata check, not a test failure). Please rename the PR to, for example: `[Perf] [NPU] multimodal: Add opt-in cross-request Qwen3-VL image batching`. I do not have permission to edit the upstream PR title/body.

### Additional Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct validation on Ascend A2

Tested the same model size as the original PR, using local `Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` weights at commit `3e50dc742b91ade64410a7543b405fbfc1feaad2`. This supplements the earlier 8B results; no repository code changes were needed.

**Environment / comparison**
- One Ascend 910B3 (64 GB), physical device 6; CANN 9.0.0, torch/torch-npu 2.10.0, Transformers 5.12.1.
- TP=1, BF16, Ascend attention with `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`, eager execution, ViT graphs disabled.
- Context length 8192, chunked prefill 4096, max running requests 64, static memory fraction 0.7.
- Same code and launch configuration for both arms; only `SGLANG_NPU_VIT_MAX_BATCH_PATCHES=0` (off) versus `16384` (on) changed.
- This is an A2 validation, **not an exact reproduction of the original CANN 9.1.0-a3 setup** or its chunk-size/memory configuration.

#### Serving performance

Used repository `python -m sglang.bench_serving`, `sglang-oai-chat` backend, image dataset, one unique random JPEG/request, input text length 32, fixed output lengths, matching seeds across arms. Each arm used a fresh server, warmed by the accuracy evaluation; each workload flushed the cache and used zero benchmark warmup requests. Two runs per workload/arm (seeds 2000–2003 and 2100–2103).

Values below are arithmetic means of the two run-level metrics (including p99, **not a pooled p99**), off → on:

| Workload | Mean TTFT (ms) | p99 TTFT (ms) | Throughput (req/s) | Mean E2E (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 448×448, output 32, concurrency 4, 64 requests/run | 449.84 → 333.63 (-25.84%) | 496.72 → 376.21 | 1.750 → 1.878 (+7.33%) | 2280.41 → 2123.16 (-6.90%) |
| 448×448, output 32, concurrency 16, 128 requests/run | 1220.21 → 711.39 (-41.70%) | 1326.59 → 841.66 | 5.021 → 4.258 (**-15.21%**) | 3169.25 → 3741.21 (**+18.05%**) |
| 448×448, output 32, concurrency 32, 128 requests/run | 2195.74 → 1002.55 (-54.34%) | 2528.64 → 1237.96 | 5.879 → 7.594 (+29.17%) | 5416.97 → 4187.20 (-22.70%) |
| 1920×1080, output 256, concurrency 16, 64 requests/run | 3545.43 → 3454.16 (-2.57%) | 5096.76 → 4978.27 | 0.763 → 0.538 (**-29.49%**) | 20858.37 → 29625.38 (**+42.03%**) |

All **1536/1536 measured requests completed**, with the expected fixed output-token counts and no OOM. Both rounds showed the same throughput direction for each workload. We did not measure peak memory in this run.

The results support keeping batching **disabled by default and opt-in**: lower TTFT does not necessarily translate into higher serving throughput or lower full-response latency. In particular, the large-image regression also occurs with 4B on this A2 setup.

#### Representative accuracy A/B

Same fixed 192-image manifest as the earlier 8B check: 64 ChartQA, 64 DocVQA, 64 VQAv2; longest edge capped at 1024, concurrency 8, temperature 0, seed 42, max output 64.

| Subset / metric | Off | On |
|---|---:|---:|
| ChartQA, 5% relaxed numeric accuracy | 81.25% | 81.25% |
| DocVQA, ANLS | 0.915833 | 0.915833 |
| VQAv2, normalized majority-answer EM (not official consensus accuracy) | 68.75% | 68.75% |

**190/192 answer strings were exactly identical**, with no truncated responses. The two differences:
- ChartQA `chart:2372`: `103.5` → `103.7`, reference `102.44`; both pass the 5% relaxed criterion.
- VQAv2 `vqa:800`: `city` → `shore`, reference `dock`; both score zero.

This small representative subset shows no score regression, but does not establish bitwise equivalence or full-benchmark accuracy.

#### Independent NPU E2E

Ran the existing registered test with `SGLANG_TEST_MODEL=/mnt/mog2/wyl/models/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, allowing it to launch its own server:
`test/registered/npu/vlm_models/test_npu_vit_batching.py`

**1 passed in 76.83 s**. This uses patch budget 2048 and chunked prefill 512, covering different image sizes, ordered multi-image answers, an oversized image, and repeated images with changed text prefixes/reversed request order.

Raw benchmark JSONL, service logs, accuracy answers, and E2E logs are retained. The test server has been stopped and device 6 released. These are local A2 results, not a claim that upstream CI or A3/A5 validation has passed.

The current PR body still describes the previous output-token budget/default; the current code uses **input patch budget `SGLANG_NPU_VIT_MAX_BATCH_PATCHES`, default 0**. Please update the description before marking ready for review.

### Collaboration update: input-patch budget + A2 validation

I have integrated the input-patch budgeting and regression coverage from #44233 into this branch as incremental, signed-off commit `3e50dc742b` (preserving the original commits).

**Configuration and scope**
- Replace the merged-output-token budget with `SGLANG_NPU_VIT_MAX_BATCH_PATCHES`, counting **input patches before spatial merging**. With merge size 2, 16384 input patches correspond to 4096 output visual tokens. Output token counts are still used to split embeddings correctly.
- **Default is 0 (disabled)**; positive values opt in. Nonpositive values disable NPU cross-request batching, rather than removing the limit. This is intentional: the A2 measurements below show workload-dependent throughput regressions.
- Retain the Qwen3-VL Dense/MoE allowlist, with conservative guards for TP=1, unquantized models, no encoder DP, and ViT graphs disabled. Unsupported configurations retain per-request encoding. CUDA batching is unchanged.
- Oversized/unknown-size images run alone; the budget is **not a hard memory cap**. Inputs are moved per group.

**A2 serving performance**

Environment: one Ascend 910B3 64 GB (A2), CANN 9.0.0, PyTorch/torch-npu 2.10.0, Transformers 5.12.1 from the A2 image, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct BF16, TP1, eager, chunked prefill 4096, context 8192, max-running-requests 64, mem-fraction-static 0.7. This is a different hardware/software/model setup from the original A3/4B measurements, so the numbers should not be compared directly.

Tool: repository-standard `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name image`; unique random JPEGs, one image/request, 32 requested text tokens, fixed output length, unlimited request rate bounded by the listed concurrency. Two rounds with matched seeds across arms; server restarted between disabled (0) and enabled (16384). Each arm was warmed by the preceding accuracy pass; per-run benchmark warmup was 0 and prefix cache was flushed. Different seeds avoid repeated-image cache hits between workloads.

Numbers below are the **arithmetic mean of two run-level summaries** (including per-run P99, not a pooled P99). These are measurements on a shared server, not confidence intervals or universal speedup guarantees.

| Workload | Requests/round | Mean TTFT ms, off → on | P99 TTFT ms, off → on | Throughput req/s, off → on | Mean E2E ms, off → on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 448×448, output 32, c4 | 64 | 471 → 378 (-19.7%) | 518 → 419 | 1.709 → 1.815 (+6.2%) | 2335 → 2197 |
| 448×448, output 32, c16 | 128 | 1487 → 859 (-42.3%) | 2793 → 990 | 4.566 → 4.279 (**-6.3%**) | 3496 → 3722 |
| 448×448, output 32, c32 | 128 | 2358 → 1328 (-43.7%) | 2729 → 1646 | 5.564 → 7.193 (+29.3%) | 5726 → 4423 |
| 1920×1080, output 256, c16 | 64 | 5482 → 5080 (-7.3%) | 8679 → 7425 | 0.671 → 0.519 (**-22.6%**) | 23740 → 30707 |

All **1536 measured requests** completed successfully, with no observed OOM. The main conclusion is improved small-image TTFT, **not** a blanket throughput improvement. In particular, the large-image regression repeated in both rounds; this is why the integration keeps the optimization opt-in. No new peak-memory claim is made.

**Paired real-image accuracy**

192 fixed images: 64 each from ChartQA, DocVQA, and VQAv2; identical inputs, concurrency 8, temperature 0, seed 42, max_tokens 64, longest image edge capped at 1024.

| Subset metric | Disabled | Enabled |
|---|---:|---:|
| ChartQA relaxed score | 0.859375 | 0.859375 |
| DocVQA ANLS | 0.920980 | 0.936605 |
| VQAv2 majority-answer EM | 0.671875 | 0.671875 |

190/192 answer strings were exactly identical. The other two changed: ChartQA 1.89 → reference 1.88 (both pass the relaxed metric), and one DocVQA wrong answer → reference “midwestern”. No API failures or truncated outputs. This is a small-subset regression check, **not** proof of universal precision parity, bitwise-equivalent embeddings, or improved general model accuracy. VQAv2 uses majority-answer EM, not the official consensus metric.

**Tests and documentation**
- CPU regression suite: **36 passed**, including input/output budget distinction, oversized/unknown shapes, cache on/off, continuation slices, default-off behavior, and mode guards.
- Single-NPU E2E: **1 passed** on A2, independently launching the final commit with budget 2048 and chunk size 512; covers mixed sizes, multi-image order, oversized images, and cache reuse.
- pre-commit, `mint validate`, and `mint broken-links`: passed.
- Added the NPU environment-variable documentation and a registered single-NPU image-association/cache E2E.

One unrelated environment caveat: the current branch's NPU image preprocessing calls the older `resize(image=...)` interface. In our isolated Transformers 5.19 environment, startup failed before batching with `Qwen2VLImageProcessor.resize() missing ... images and factor`; the A2 image's Transformers 5.12.1 works. No preprocessing compatibility patch is included in this integration.
